title: Area and Perimeter: Polygons, Circles and Composite Shapes
seo_title: Grade 9 Area and Perimeter Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_code: Grade 9: 4.1 Area and perimeter of 2D shapes
standard_text: Use appropriate formulae to calculate perimeter and area of polygons and circles; investigate how doubling any or all the dimensions of a 2-D figure affects its perimeter and its area; solve problems involving perimeter and area of polygons and circles.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 9 area and perimeter worksheets: trapeziums, kites, circles, parts of circles and composite shapes. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: A = πr²; trapezium A = ½(a + b)h.
key_sub: Subtract the area of a hole.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Trapezium: A = ½(a + b)h. Kite and rhombus: A = ½ × d₁ × d₂.
  • Circle: C = 2πr, A = πr².
  • A semicircle has half the area of the circle.
  • For a shape with a hole, subtract the area of the hole.

Examples

Example

A square of side 10 cm with a circular hole of radius 3 cm

100 − π × 9

Answer: about 71,7 cm²

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Forgetting ½Trapeziums and kites need ½.
Diameter as radiusr = d ÷ 2.
Adding the holeSubtract it.
